question: The famous building 'Qutub Minar' has been built under which style of architecture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mamulek Style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Qutub Minar is an iconic monument constructed under the **Mamulek (or Mamluk) style of architecture**, which is a part of the Delhi Sultanate architectural tradition.
 
• It was commissioned by **Qutb al-Din Aibak**, the founder of the Delhi Sultanate, in 1192, and later completed by his successors.
 
• This architectural style is characterized by the use of red sandstone, intricate carvings, and calligraphic inscriptions, often incorporating Islamic motifs and verses from the Quran.
 
• The Qutub Minar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and stands at a height of **72.5 meters**, making it one of the tallest minarets in the world built of bricks.
 
• The Mamulek style of architecture often blended Islamic and indigenous Indian elements, creating a unique fusion evident in monuments like the Qutub Minar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mamulek Architecture:**

 
 
• Also known as Mamluk architecture, it emerged during the reign of the Slave Dynasty (1206–1290) in India.
 
• It extensively used locally available materials like red sandstone while incorporating Islamic architectural features such as arches, domes, and minarets.
 
• Floral patterns, arabesques, and geometric designs were a hallmark of this style.
 
 
 
• **Qutub Minar Construction:**
 
 
• Qutb al-Din Aibak began its construction, but it was completed by his successor, Iltutmish.
 
• It is surrounded by several historically significant structures, including the Iron Pillar and Alai Darwaza.
 
• The minar has five distinct storeys, each marked by projecting balconies and intricate carvings.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate Architecture:**
 
 
• It refers to the architectural developments during the rule of the Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526).
 
• It includes other notable structures like the Alai Darwaza, the tomb of Iltutmish, and the Tughlaqabad Fort.
 
• This style laid the foundation for later Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**
 
 
• The Qutub Minar complex was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.
 
• It is recognized for its historical, architectural, and cultural significance.
